newsitem.title: USA: Maine governor unveils plan to stem tax increases.
newsitem.headline: Maine governor unveils plan to stem tax increases.

text.p: Maine Gov. Angus King on Wednesday unveiled a complex proposal to stem future tax increases by requiring that the total tax burden be determined before the state's budget is drafted.
King told reporters the plan would reduce the overall burden of state and local taxes, which he maintains has hampered economic development and fueled excessive governmental growth.
"This is a proposal to put government on a diet," King told reporters. The measure must be approved by the legislature, which is expected to consider the plan Thursday.

Under the plan, an advisory committee would set pre-budget targets for total tax burden, how the burden will be divided between state and local taxes and how the state would raise its portion through its various levies.

The plan would require the governor to draft a budget consistent with the committee's recomendation. King said the legislature should also follow revenue targets, but he acknowledged there was no legal way to make lawmakers do that.
Half of revenues collected in excess of the original revenue target would be put in the state's Rainy Day Fund.

King said the percentage of Maine's total income claimed by state and local taxes increased from 10.7 percent in 1985 to 12.7 percent in 1995 -- giving the state one of the highest tax burdens in the United States.

The governor said his proposal would still allow local governments to set their own budgets, but communities that allow revenue growth to exceed the target would have their share of state aid decline by an equal amount.
